This R markdown script demonstrates the practical use of our proposed helper functions to estimate incremental costs between two groups in a realistic dataset.

- **`glmx_start()`** estimates starting values to overcomes errors (glm, glm2) or suboptimal fits (glmmTMB).
- **`get_best_model()`** returns the model with the lowest AIC from all converged models (non-NULL, converged, and valid AIC).
- **`glmx()`** fits multiple regression models using four different packages (`stats::glm(), glm2::glm2(), mgcv::gam(), glmmTMB::glmmTMB()`) and returns the best fitting model.
- **`glmx_events()`** fits multiple regression models for the first stage of a two stage model (number of events with non-zero costs) using Poisson with identity and log-link, and returns the best fitting model.
- **`glmx_pcosts()`** fits multiple regression models for the second stage of a two stage model (positive costs) using Gamma with identity and log-link, and returns the best fitting model.
- **`marginal_one_stage()`** predicts marginal cost difference between groups for a single stage model based on a population sample (here, the study sample).
- **`marginal_two_stage()`** predicts marginal cost difference between groups for a two stage model based on a population sample (here, the study sample).

## Robust Regressions

Infrastructure and utility functions (skip ahead to example usage)

```{r robust_regressions}
  # overcomes glm/glm2 (log-link) error "no valid set of coefficients has been found: please supply starting values"
  glmx_start <- function(formula, data, family) {
    m <- lm(formula, data)
    c <- coef(m)
    if (family$link == "identity") {
      c[names(c) == "(Intercept)"] <- mean(predict(m))
      c[names(c) != "(Intercept)"] <- 0.0
    } else if (family$link == "log") {
      c[names(c) == "(Intercept)"] <- log(mean(predict(m)))
      c[names(c) != "(Intercept)"] <- 0.0
    } else {
      c[] <- 1.0
    }
    return(c)
  }

  # utility function to select best regression fit, instrumented to track performance
  get_best_model <- function(m_list) {
    returned  <- map_lgl(m_list,  ~       !is.null(.x))
    converged <- map_lgl(m_list,  ~ifelse(!is.null(.x), class(.x)[1] == "lm" || (class(.x)[1] %in% c("glm", "gam") && .x$converged[1]) || (class(.x)[1] == "glmmTMB" && .x$fit$convergence == 0), FALSE))
    AICs      <- map_dbl(m_list,  ~ifelse(!is.null(.x), AIC(.x), NA))
    valid_AIC <- converged & !is.na(AICs)
    if (sum(valid_AIC) == 0) { return(NULL) }
    best_AIC <- which.min(AICs)
    m_list[[best_AIC]]$returned  <- returned
    m_list[[best_AIC]]$converged <- converged
    m_list[[best_AIC]]$valid_AIC <- valid_AIC
    m_list[[best_AIC]]$best_AIC  <- ifelse(!is.na(AICs), AICs == min(AICs, na.rm = TRUE), FALSE)
    return(m_list[[best_AIC]])
  }

  # wrapper function around glm, glm2::glm2, mgcv::gam, and glmmTMB::glmmTMB, selecting the best among multiple fits
  glmx <- function(formula, data, family) {
    s <- glmx_start(formula, data, family)
    models <- list(NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL)
    try (models[[1]] <-     glm(formula, family, data, start = s))
    try (models[[2]] <-    glm2(formula, family, data, start = s))
    try (models[[3]] <-     gam(formula, family, data))
    try (models[[4]] <- glmmTMB(formula, data, family, start = list(beta = s), na.action = na.exclude))
    return(get_best_model(models))
  }

  # wrapper to select the best fit among poisson, the latter with identity link or log-link, for counts
  glmx_events <- function(formula, data) {
    models <- list(NULL, NULL)
    try(models[[1]] <- glmx(formula, data, family = poisson(link = "identity")))
    try(models[[2]] <- glmx(formula, data, family = poisson(link = "log")))
    return(get_best_model(models))
  }

  # wrapper to select the best fit among gamma regressions with identity link or log-link, for positive costs
  glmx_pcosts <- function(formula, data) {
    models <- list(NULL, NULL)
    try(models[[1]] <- glmx(formula, data, family = Gamma(link = "identity")))
    try(models[[2]] <- glmx(formula, data, family = Gamma(link = "log")))
    return(get_best_model(models))
  }

  # utility function to extract marginal cost difference for single stage model evaluated on target population (can be the study population)
  marginal_one_stage <- function(pop, m1, model) {
    costdiff <- NA
    try(costdiff <- mean(predict(m1, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "intervention"), type = "response")) -
                    mean(predict(m1, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "control"),      type = "response")))
    return(data.frame(costdiff, model))
  }

  # utility function to extract marginal cost difference for Gaussian/Poisson-Gamma model evaluated on target population (can be the study population)
  marginal_two_stage <- function(pop, m1, m2, model) {
    costdiff <- NA
    try(costdiff <- mean(predict(m1, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "intervention"), type = "response") * predict(m2, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "intervention"), type = "response")) -
                    mean(predict(m1, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "control"),      type = "response") * predict(m2, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "control"),      type = "response")))
    return(data.frame(costdiff, model))
  }
```

## Real-World Dataset

**Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality**

- Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS) https://meps.ahrq.gov/mepsweb/ for 2024
- Variables: IPDIS (number of inpatient hospital discharges), IPFTCH (inpatient hospital charges), INSCOV (insurance status), POVCAT (income category), DATAYEAR, AGELAST, SEX, and BORNUSA
- No weighting is performed
- MEPS codes missing values as negative numbers, and any such records are excluded
- Only records with (0 costs and 0 stays) or with (positive stays and positive costs) are included
- Costs are shifted by +0.01 USD for Gaussian(log) and Gamma regressions (pcost)
- Costs per event (ecost) are defined as the cost per inpatient discharge, and they are used as the outcome of the second stage of the two-stage model

```{r dataset}
  source_file <- "https://meps.ahrq.gov/mepsweb/data_files/pufs/h256/h256xlsx.zip"
  target_file <- "./h256.xlsx"
  if (!file.exists(target_file)) {
    temp_file <- tempfile(); download.file(source_file, temp_file, method = "auto"); unzip(temp_file, overwrite = TRUE, junkpaths = TRUE); unlink(temp_file)
  } 
  study_pop <- read_xlsx(target_file) %>%
    select(N = matches("^IPDIS"), cost = matches("^IPFTCH"), INSURANCE = matches("^INSCOV"), INCOME = matches("^POVCAT"), DATAYEAR, AGELAST, SEX, BORNUSA) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~ifelse(.x < 0, NA, .x))) %>% filter(AGELAST >= 18)
  print(sprintf("MEPS %s: Adults, Observations = %d, Complete = %d (used, assuming MCAR)", paste(unique(study_pop$DATAYEAR), collapse = ", "), nrow(study_pop), nrow(study_pop %>% filter(complete.cases(.)))))
  study_pop <- study_pop %>% filter(complete.cases(.))
  print(sprintf("Removed = %d because !((N == 0 & cost == 0.0) | (N > 0 & cost > 0.0))", nrow(study_pop %>% filter(!((N == 0 & cost == 0.0) | (N > 0 & cost > 0.0))))))
  study_pop <- study_pop %>% filter((N == 0 & cost == 0.0) | (N > 0 & cost > 0.0)) %>%
    mutate(SEX       = factor(SEX,       levels = 1:2, labels = c("Male", "Female"))) %>%
    mutate(INSURANCE = factor(INSURANCE, levels = 1:3, labels = c("1: Private", "2: Public", "3: Uninsured"))) %>%
    mutate(INCOME    = factor(INCOME,    levels = 1:5, labels = c("1: Poor", "2: Near poor", "3: Low", "4: Middle", "5: High"))) %>%
    mutate(BORNUSA   = factor(BORNUSA,   levels = 1:2, labels = c("Born in USA", "Born outside USA"))) %>%
    mutate(pcost     = cost + 0.01, ecost = cost / pmax(N, 1)) %>%
    mutate(study_group = ifelse(BORNUSA == "Born in USA", "control", "intervention"))
  study_pop %>% group_by(BORNUSA) %>% reframe(N_Group = n(), Mean_USD = sum(cost) / sum(N), Prop_0_Cost = sprintf("%.01f %%", 100.0 * sum(cost == 0.0) / n())) %>% flextable() %>% autofit()
```

## Example Usage

**Note:** Warnings are expected as we anticipate some models to fail

Regression models are adjusted for sex, age in years, income category, and insurance status

```{r example, warning = FALSE}
  # compute different regression models
  m_Gauss     <-   lm(        cost ~ study_group + SEX + AGELAST + INCOME + INSURANCE, data = study_pop)                               # Gaussian identity link, unmodified cost
  m_Gamma_log <- glmx(       pcost ~ study_group + SEX + AGELAST + INCOME + INSURANCE, data = study_pop, family = Gamma(link = "log")) # Gamma log link, cost shifted by 0.01 USD
  m_Events    <- glmx_events(    N ~ study_group + SEX + AGELAST + INCOME + INSURANCE, data = study_pop)                               # first stage: number of events
  m_Ecosts    <- glmx_pcosts(ecost ~ study_group + SEX + AGELAST + INCOME + INSURANCE, data = study_pop %>% filter(N > 0))             # second stage: cost per event, only if event

  # check convergence and best AIC (arrays for glm* implementations from different packages) and identity-link vs. log-link
  print("Convergence")
  print(paste("Gamma log-link   (glm, glm2, gam, glmmTMB):",         paste(m_Gamma_log$converged, collapse = ", ")))
  print(paste("Number of Events (Poisson identity-link, log-link):", paste(m_Events$converged,    collapse = ", ")))
  print(paste("Costs per event  (Gamma   identity-link, log-link):", paste(m_Ecosts$converged,    collapse = ", ")))
  print("Best AIC")
  print(paste("Gamma log-link   (glm, glm2, gam, glmmTMB):",         paste(m_Gamma_log$best_AIC, collapse = ", ")))
  print(paste("Number of Events (Poisson identity-link, log-link):", paste(m_Events$best_AIC,    collapse = ", ")))
  print(paste("Costs per event  (Gamma   identity-link, log-link):", paste(m_Ecosts$best_AIC,    collapse = ", ")))
```

## Results

```{r results, warning = FALSE}
  # utility function to report marginal risk differences (RD) from comparisons
  marginal_RD <- function(m1, digits = 2) {
    rd <- as.data.frame(comparisons(m1, comparison = "difference", by = TRUE, type = "response")) %>%
      mutate(estimate = sprintf("%.0*f [%.0*f; %.0*f]", digits, estimate, digits, conf.low, digits, conf.high)) %>%
      mutate(contrast = str_replace_all(contrast, c("intervention" = "Born outside USA", "control" = "Born in USA"))) %>%
      select(term, contrast, estimate)
    return(rd)
  }

  # compute marginal cost difference for all regression models
  Gauss_id  <- marginal_one_stage(study_pop, m_Gauss,     "Single-stage: Gaussian (identity link)")
  Gamma_log <- marginal_one_stage(study_pop, m_Gamma_log, "Single-stage: Gamma (log link)")
  Two_Stage <- marginal_two_stage(study_pop, m_Events, m_Ecosts, "Two-stage: Poisson * Gamma")
  rbind(Gauss_id, Gamma_log, Two_Stage) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ sprintf("%.02f", .x))) %>% flextable() %>% autofit() %>% set_caption("Marginal differences in cost [USD]: Born outside vs. in USA")
  marginal_RD(m_Events, 3) %>% flextable() %>% autofit() %>% set_caption("Marginal differences in number of events per annum")
  marginal_RD(m_Ecosts)    %>% flextable() %>% autofit() %>% set_caption("Marginal differences in cost per event [USD]")
  marginal_RD(m_Gauss)     %>% flextable() %>% autofit() %>% set_caption("Marginal differences in cost [USD]: Gaussian(identity)")
  marginal_RD(m_Gamma_log) %>% flextable() %>% autofit() %>% set_caption("Marginal differences in cost [USD]: Gamma(log)")
```
